message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles along the I‑5 corridor covers roughly **380–400 miles** (about 610–640 km). Under normal conditions—steady traffic, no major detours, and staying within speed limits—the trip typically takes **around 6 to 7 hours**.

**Things that can affect the duration:**

| Factor | Impact on Time |
|--------|----------------|
| **Traffic congestion** (especially near the Bay Area, Sacramento, or the Los Angeles metro) | Adds 30 min–2 hrs |
| **Roadwork / construction** | Adds 15 min–1 hr |
| **Weather** (fog, rain, snow) | Adds 10 min–30 min |
| **Speed limits** (I‑5 is usually 65–75 mph, but can drop to 55 mph in urban areas) | Determines baseline speed |
| **Stops** (fuel, food, rest) | Adds 15 min–1 hr per stop |

If you’re planning a trip, it’s a good idea to check real‑time traffic updates (e.g., Google Maps, Waze) before you leave and consider leaving early in the morning or late at night to avoid peak traffic times.
